thread:
jess: Quick flag — noticed quickstart README has inconsistent env var names and a copy/paste pain for new users. Repro: the curl example uses `Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API` but the Python and Node snippets expect `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Users are pasting the curl example and then hitting auth errors.
jess: curl snippet from README:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"hi"}'
```

jess: Python snippet elsewhere uses:
```py
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
```

jess: So the env var name mismatch is a straight footgun. Also the curl example's placeholder looks like a token but not matching our ENV convention. We should be consistent and make snippets copy-paste friendly (and add a one-liner in the README about exporting env var).

sam: Thanks for catching this — agreed it's causing onboarding friction. I can open a quick PR to standardize on `REDWOOD_API_KEY` across examples and change the curl example to `Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY` (and add a short note showing `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...`).

sam: Also flag: the Node quickstart in the same doc uses `import Redwood from 'redwood'` but our SDK uses a named export `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood'` so copy/paste breaks for users using ESM/CommonJS interop. I'd like to fix that too.

alex: Good catch on the Node import — saw a support ticket. Suggested Node snippet:
```js
// ESM
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })

// CommonJS
const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
```

maria: I can take the PR and also add a tiny snippet test to our docs CI that does a regex check for `REDWOOD_API_KEY` presence in all quickstart snippets so we catch drift. Will also add the `export` example and a one-line explanation of env var precedence.

jess: Awesome. Can we also add a note near the curl snippet recommending `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\"` rather than pasting a raw token? Small UX win.

sam: Yep — opening PR now. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 (will update title). Changes: unify env var to `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, fix Node/TS examples, add one-line env export, and small CI snippet check.

maria: I reviewed locally, added the snippet-check script, and pushed changes to the PR branch. Also updated the README diff to ensure fenced blocks show explicit language tags (helps tooling). cc @docs-bot for doc lint.
